artifacts.name: D-masked germlines · Artificial immunization: three families
artifacts.method: Family allele intersection and AIRR CIGAR projection
artifacts.describe: D-masked reference reconstruction within each saved family and locus. Explicit V/J allele calls must have one common allele. AIRR CIGARs project ungapped reference segments onto the oriented query; all intervening D/N/P bases are N. Indels remain gaps. This is not an inferred genotype, unmutated junction or lineage ancestor; no mutation rate is computed.

artifacts.name: Somatic hypermutation · Artificial immunization: three families
artifacts.method: Observed nucleotide divergence; single-hit R/S attribution
artifacts.describe: Observed nucleotide differences from the saved D-masked V/J reference, per source chain row; not historical mutation events or a mutation rate. Only paired A/C/G/T bases enter the denominator. Masks, ambiguities and gaps are separate. Regions use supplied oriented-query coordinates. Codons require checked CDR3/junction phase, vj_in_frame=true and an indel-free projection; complete non-stop codons within one segment are compared using NCBI table 1. Replacement/silent substitutions are attributed only in single-hit codons; multiple-hit codons have endpoint amino-acid classifications but their substitutions remain unclassified. Sample/locus summaries pool counts across source rows, without abundance weighting, deduplication or inferential statistics.

artifacts.name: Lineage trees · Artificial immunization: three families
artifacts.describe: Equal-cost nucleotide parsimony within each saved family/locus, rooted at its V/J reference on a shared, complete-case reference-coordinate panel. D/N/P, gaps, ambiguity and uncovered sites are omitted; identical panel states collapse without abundance weighting. At most 8 taxa including the reference are searched exhaustively; 9–64 use three deterministic addition orders and strict-improvement NNI, capped at 50000 candidate scores and 200 million pattern-node work units. Heuristic scores are not proven global minima. One reproducible binary topology and one consistent minimum-change ancestral assignment are shown, with marginal IUPAC state sets conditional on that topology. Exact split counts describe tied optimal binary trees, not bootstrap support or probabilities. Zero-length edges and binary resolutions do not establish distinct ancestors. Observed isotypes, timepoints and tissues do not constrain topology or infer switching, migration or event dates.

artifacts.name: Isotypes · Artificial immunization: three families
artifacts.method: Observed constant-region usage and unordered family co-occurrence
artifacts.describe: Observed heavy-chain constant-region usage within a saved, thresholded family result. Each assigned observation contributes once: a sample-scoped cell in single-cell data, a heavy-chain source row in bulk data. All retained heavy C calls must be supported and agree at the reported resolution; allele ties are collapsed, same-class subclass ties retain class only, and missing, unsupported or conflicting calls remain unresolved. Light chains do not define isotype. Observation shares include unresolved assigned observations in the denominator; parent-excluded observations stay outside it. Abundance belongs to the observation, never to each source chain; a missing count makes its bucket and the group's abundance denominator unavailable. Family pairs count unordered co-occurrence of resolved constant genes once per family. They do not count switching events or establish direction, timing, ancestral isotypes, rates or significance. IgM/IgD co-occurrence alone is not switching evidence. Sample annotations are pinned; no timepoints, tissues or subjects are pooled as biological replicates.
